summary: Created a dedicated systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 running a long-lived background worker as an unprivileged system user (`inventory`), sandboxed with NoNewPrivileges=yes and filesystem confinement (root filesystem read-only via ProtectSystem=full + ReadOnlyDirectories=/, with only /var/lib/inventory writable via ReadWriteDirectories=). Verified the worker persistently writes only inside /var/lib/inventory. Completed the mandatory node1 restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and healthy service/data state, issued a native reboot, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified the service auto-recovered (active/enabled) with data continuing to accumulate and sandbox mounts intact after restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04, systemd 229) and confirmed non-interactive sudo access
Created system user 'inventory' (no login, no home) and directory /var/lib/inventory owned by it (mode 0750)
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh, a POSIX sh loop that writes a counter and log file inside /var/lib/inventory every 10s

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service running as User=inventory/Group=inventory with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ReadOnlyDirectories=/, ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory, PrivateTmp=yes, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateDevices=yes (pre-v231 directive names, compatible with systemd 229)
Enabled and started the service; verified active state, PID, and data being written

Verified confinement via the running process's /proc/PID/mountinfo: root filesystem mounted ro, /var/lib/inventory mounted as a separate rw bind mount; confirmed systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes configured
Captured baseline boot_id, service active/enabled state, and counter/log contents before restart
Issued 'sudo shutdown -r now' in background on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed from 35c87ec9-1707-4fb3-ab1d-f264d3618caa to f72b61b0-fe7b-476c-bc8a-42b37190b968, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: service active and enabled, counter/log continuing to increment, and root-ro / /var/lib/inventory-rw mount confinement still intact

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker running as a managed (systemd) service
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows inventory-worker.service loaded, enabled, and active (running) with correct ExecStart process tree

Directory /var/lib/inventory created owned by dedicated inventory user; live process mountinfo shows root '/' mounted read-only while /var/lib/inventory is a separate read-write bind mount; write attempt to /etc as the inventory user fails with Permission denied while write inside /var/lib/inventory succeeds

systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes is configured on the unit; procfs on this kernel does not expose a NoNewPrivs field even for PID 1, so its absence for the worker is not evidence against the setting

evidence.requirement: Worker is long-running / actively producing data
evidence.summary: Worker script loops indefinitely; counter and inventory.log inside /var/lib/inventory increment every ~10s across repeated checks
Captured pre-restart boot_id 35c87ec9-1707-4fb3-ab1d-f264d3618caa, service active/enabled, and counter=6 with recent log ticks
Issued backgrounded 'sudo shutdown -r now'; command returned its PID/acknowledgement before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node briefly unreachable (SSH connection refused) during reboot, then reachable again with a new boot_id f72b61b0-fe7b-476c-bc8a-42b37190b968, differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: recovered state and data
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: inventory-worker.service is active and enabled again, counter continued incrementing (7->9) and log kept appending, and mountinfo confirms root-ro/var-lib-inventory-rw confinement persisted after restart
